properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 9 at 11:55PM EDT until October 12 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued
a Flood Advisory for the following rivers in North Carolina...

French Broad River Near at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W Fletcher
affecting Buncombe and Henderson Counties.

.Heavy rainfall from the remnants of Hurricane Isaias will result in
excessive runoff and significant rises on streams within the upper
French Broad River watershed.  Rainfall will develop overnight
tonight, intensify during the day on Saturday, and maintain intensity
through early Sunday morning before tapering off by Sunday
mid-morning.  Storm-total rainfall of 4-8 inches is expected, with
isolated 8-10 inches possible, across the upper French Broad River
watershed, generally upstream of Etowah.  The highest totals will
occur along the Tanassee and Pisgah ridges, with lesser amounts
within the upper French Broad River valley.  Additionally, 4-6 inches
of rainfall are expected within the Mud Creek watershed in Henderson
County, which is a primary tributary of the French Broad River above
Fletcher.  While there continues to be some uncertainty regarding the
exact location, timing, and amounts of the heaviest rainfall, there
is enough confidence in the current forecast that out-of-bank
conditions are likely for the upper French Broad River.  Therefore, a
River Flood Advisory has been issued for the reach near Fletcher,
with a crest above Action Stage expected around Sunday afternoon.  A
rise above Action Stage will result in nuisance, relatively shallow
flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to the Broad River, including
farmland, woodlands, low-lying secondary roads, greenways, parks, and
other flood-prone locations.  Additional River Flood Advisories are
possible Saturday, especially for the French Broad River reach near
Blantyre.

More significant rises along the French Broad River are possible, and
those with interests along the river are encouraged to stay weather
aware and up-to-date on the latest stream levels and forecasts at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/GSP.  Current reasonable worst-case
scenarios are posted in the ADDITIONAL DETAILS sections below.
Forecast crests above Minor Flood Stage may result in the River Flood
Advisories being upgraded to River Flood Warnings.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...French Broad River near at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W
Fletcher.

* WHEN...From this evening to Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Action/Advisory Stage.  The French Broad
River has exceeded bankfull at the gauge site.  Isolated farmland
flooding is beginning across the French Broad River Valley from
Etowah downstream to Avery Creek upstream of the gauge site. At
11.5 feet, Action Stage Flooding continues.  Butler Bridge Rd. is
inundated with up to 6 inches of floodwaters from the French Broad
River, forcing road closure.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 PM EDT Friday the stage was 3.6 feet and steady.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 10.6 feet
early Sunday afternoon.  A crest closer to 12 feet is possible.
A reasonable worst-case crest above Minor Flood Stage below 15
feet cannot be ruled out.
- Action/Advisory Stage is 10.0 feet.
- Minor Flood Stage is 13.0 feet.

properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued October 9 at 8:43PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
HLSSGX

This product covers EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA

**Tropical Storm Rachel Will Bring Coastal Flooding, Wind, and Rain to
Portions of Southern California Sunday**


NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for San Diego County
Coastal Areas, San Diego County Deserts, San Diego County
Mountains, and San Diego County Valleys

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 740 miles south-southwest of San Mateo Point CA or about
710 miles south-southwest of Mouth of Tijuana River CA
- 23.8N 123.3W
- Storm Intensity 45 mph
- Movement Northeast or 50 degrees at 9 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Rachel is currently just over 700 miles southwest of
San Diego, moving northeast towards Northern Baja. Rachel is expected
to make landfall somewhere near the US/Mexico Border late Saturday
night. Tropical storm level impacts have the potential to impact San
Diego County. A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for all of San Diego
County. The main concerns with Tropical Storm Rachel are coastal
flooding, wind, and periods of heavy rain. The majority of impacts from
the tropical storm are expected on Sunday.

South swell from Tropical Storm Rachel will arrive on Sunday. The
combination of south and northwest swells, increased onshore winds,
and high tides over 7 feet will maintain a threat of coastal flooding
and beach erosion along beaches in San Diego County. Surf on Sunday is
currently expected to peak at 5 to 8 feet with sets to 9 feet,
decreasing to 3 to 6 feet for Monday and Tuesday. Confidence in
impactful coastal flooding is high, with significant coastal flooding
and beach erosion likely.

Widespread rain is expected on Sunday from Tropical Storm Rachel.
There is expected to be a gradient in rainfall amounts with the higher
amounts on the southeastern side of the storm. We have the highest
confidence that the heaviest rain will occur over San Diego County
mountains and deserts. Peak rainfall rates of 0.50 to 0.60 inches are
possible for the coast and valleys, 0.50 to 0.70 inches per hour
possible for the deserts, and 0.70 to 1 inch per hour for the
mountains. Current forecast has rainfall totals of 0.50 to 1.25 inches
for the coast, valleys, and deserts and 1 to 2.5 inches for the
mountains. Areas of flash and urban flooding are possible, especially
where the maximum rainfall rates occur. The San Diego River at Fashion
Valley is currently forecast to peak at 7.4 feet (just below monitor
stage) Sunday afternoon. Those with interests near the San Diego River
should continue to monitor the forecast.

Increased winds are expected with the onset and passage of Tropical
Storm Rachel. Sustained winds of 39+ mph are expected on the southeast
side of the storm. Based on the current track, more southern and
eastern parts of the county are most likely to see winds of this
magnitude. Regardless, strong sustained winds and wind gusts can be
expected on Sunday. Winds may be enhanced by local terrain with gusts
40 to 55 mph on the desert slopes of the mountains and into the
deserts. Local gusts up to 60 mph possible on mountain ridges.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Prepare for hazardous wind having possible limited impacts across
EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA. Potential impacts include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted, especially in coastal and valley locations that
don't typically experience strong winds. Some fences and
roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Prepare for life-threatening rainfall flooding having possible
extensive impacts across San Diego County. Potential impacts include:
- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in
multiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, arroyos, and
ditches may become dangerous rivers. In mountain areas,
destructive runoff may run quickly down valleys while
increasing susceptibility to rockslides and mudslides. Flood
control systems and barriers may become stressed.
- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed
away. Many places where flood waters may cover escape routes.
Streets and parking lots become rivers of moving water with
underpasses submerged. Driving conditions become dangerous.
Many road and bridge closures with some weakened or washed out.

Prepare for dangerous rainfall flooding having possible significant
impacts across San Diego County.

* OTHER COASTAL HAZARDS:
High tides over 7 ft, combined with high surf and gusty onshore winds
will increase the threat for coastal flooding across area beaches.
Additionally surf of 6 to 9 ft will create dangerous swimming
conditions. There is increasing potential for significant coastal
flooding and beach erosion.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
If you live in a place particularly vulnerable to flooding, such as
low-elevation areas near the ocean, in a low-lying or poor drainage
area, or in a valley, plan to move to safe shelter on higher ground.

Now is the time to check your emergency plan and emergency supplies
kit and take necessary actions to protect your family and secure your
home or business.

Always heed the advice of local officials and comply with orders that
are issued.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather Radio and local news
outlets for official storm information. Listen for possible changes
to the forecast.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in San Diego CA around 2 AM PDT, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

NWSheadline:
Tropical Storm Rachel Will Bring Coastal Flooding, Wind, and Rain to
Portions of Southern California Sunday

properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued October 9 at 10:35PM CDT by NWS Jackson MS
properties.description:
HLSJAN

This product covers Central Mississippi, Northeast Louisiana, and extreme Southeast Arkansas

HURRICANE ISAIAS HAS MADE LANDFALL ON THE FLORIDA COAST

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Choctaw, Clarke,
Clay, Forrest, Jasper, Jones, Kemper, Lauderdale, Lowndes,
Neshoba, Newton, Noxubee, Oktibbeha, Webster, and Winston

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 170 miles east of Hattiesburg MS or about 240 miles
east-southeast of Jackson MS
- 30.8N 86.5W
- Storm Intensity 90 mph
- Movement North or 5 degrees at 20 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Hurricane Isaias has made landfall as a hurricane near Destin
Florida this evening. Though Isaias will gradually weaken as it
moves north across Alabama overnight into Saturday, tropical storm
force wind gusts are possible across portions of East and Northeast
Mississippi.  Gradient wind will increase this evening in
southeastern Mississippi, then stronger gusts are expected overnight
into Saturday across eastern and northeastern Mississippi. Downed
trees and power outages are expected in these areas. Heavy rainfall
and flash flooding are also possible, mainly in the Golden Triangle
area. Threat has trended overall downward. Conditions will improve
late Saturday afternoon into Saturday evening.


POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Protect against hazardous wind having possible limited impacts across
eastern and northeastern Mississippi. Potential impacts in this area
include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Central Mississippi, Northeast Louisiana, and
extreme Southeast Arkansas, little to no impact is anticipated.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Protect against dangerous rainfall flooding having possible
significant impacts across the Golden Triangle area. Potential
impacts include:
- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations and
rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly become swollen with swifter
currents and overspill their banks in a few places, especially
in usually vulnerable spots. Small streams, creeks, canals, and
ditches overflow.
- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken foundations.
Several places may experience expanded areas of rapid
inundation at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Some streets and parking lots take on moving water as
storm drains and retention ponds overflow. Driving conditions
become hazardous. Some road and bridge closures.

Protect against locally hazardous rainfall flooding having possible
limited impacts across East Mississippi.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.


* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to complete all preparations to protect life and
property in accordance with your emergency plan. Ensure you are in a
safe location before the onset of strong winds or possible flooding.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather radio or local news outlets
for official storm information. Be ready to adapt to possible changes
to the forecast. Ensure you have multiple ways to receive weather
warnings.


* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Jackson MS around 4 AM, or sooner if conditions warrant.

properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued October 9 at 10:31PM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
HLSMOB

This product covers portions of southwest Alabama...northwest Florida...south
central Alabama...and inland southeast Mississippi.

**ISAIAS MOVING OVER THE WESTERN FLORIDA PANHANDLE INTO SOUTH CENTRAL ALABAMA**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Storm Surge Warning and Hurricane Warning are in effect for
Baldwin Central, Baldwin Coastal, Escambia Coastal, Mobile
Central, Mobile Coastal, Okaloosa Coastal, and Santa Rosa
Coastal
- A Hurricane Warning is in effect for Baldwin Inland, Butler,
Conecuh, Covington, Crenshaw, Escambia, Escambia Inland, Mobile
Inland, Monroe, Okaloosa Inland, and Santa Rosa Inland
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Choctaw, Clarke,
George, Greene, Perry, Stone, Washington, Wayne, and Wilcox

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 100 miles east of Mobile AL or about 50 miles
east-northeast of Pensacola FL
- 30.8N 86.5W
- Storm Intensity 90 mph
- Movement North or 5 degrees at 20 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Hurricane Isaias with winds of 90 mph will continue to move north at
near 20 mph into south central Alabama. Significant wind impacts and
life threatening storm surge will remain through late tonight. The
strongest winds will occur near and just to the east of the center,
and storm surge inundation of 5 to 7 feet above normally dry ground
will persist along the coast of the western Florida panhandle.
Potential impacts from these winds include numerous downed trees and
power lines, significant power outages, and some roof damage.

Additional rainfall totals of 2 to 4 inches with localized amounts of
6 inches are possible east of the Alabama River. Areas of flooding are
likely if the higher amounts are realized, with considerable impacts
possible.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Protect against life-threatening wind having possible devastating
impacts across the western Florida Panhandle and south central Alabama.
Potential  impacts in this area include:
- Structural damage to sturdy buildings, some with complete roof
and wall failures. Complete destruction of mobile homes. Damage
greatly accentuated by large airborne projectiles. Locations
may be uninhabitable for weeks or months.
- Numerous large trees snapped or uprooted along with fences and
roadway signs blown over.
- Many roads impassable from large debris, and more within urban
or heavily wooded places.
- Widespread power and communications outages.

Also, protect against life-threatening wind having possible limited
to extensive impacts across inland southeast Mississippi and southwest
Alabama.

* SURGE:
Protect against life-threatening surge having possible significant
impacts across the coastal portions of the western Florida panhandle
and Alabama. Potential impacts in this area include:
- Areas of inundation with storm surge flooding accentuated by
waves. Damage to several buildings, mainly near the coast.
- Sections of near-shore escape routes and secondary roads become
weakened or washed out, especially in usually vulnerable low
spots.
- Major beach erosion with heavy surf breaching dunes. Strong and
numerous rip currents.
- Moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks, and piers.
Several small craft broken away from moorings, especially in
unprotected anchorages.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Protect against life-threatening rainfall flooding having possible
extensive impacts across south central Alabama and the western Florida
panhandle. Potential impacts include:
- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in
multiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches may
become dangerous rivers. Flood control systems and barriers may
become stressed.
- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed
away. Many places where flood waters may cover escape routes.
Streets and parking lots become rivers of moving water with
underpasses submerged. Driving conditions become dangerous.
Many road and bridge closures with some weakened or washed out.

Protect against dangerous rainfall flooding having possible limited
to significant impacts across interior southeast Mississippi.

* TORNADOES:
Little to no impacts are anticipated at this time across the area.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
It is important to remain calm, informed, and focused during an
emergency. Be patient and helpful with those you encounter.

Rapidly rising flood waters are deadly. If you are in a flood-prone
area, consider moving to higher ground. Never drive through a flooded
roadway. Remember, turn around don't drown!

If in a place that is vulnerable to high wind, such as near large
trees, a manufactured home, upper floors of a high-rise building, or
on a boat, consider moving to a safer shelter before the onset of
strong winds or flooding.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather radio or local news outlets
for official storm information. Be ready to adapt to possible changes
to the forecast. Ensure you have multiple ways to receive weather
warnings.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For the latest detailed evacuation and shelter information...please
refer to your local emergency management agency at the phone number
or website listed below.
- Coastal Alabama:
- Baldwin County: 251-972-6807 or
www.baldwincountyal.gov/departments/EMA
- Mobile County: 251-460-8000 or mobilecountyema.gov
- Northwest Florida:
- Escambia County: 850-471-6400 or myescambia.com/beready
- Santa Rosa County: 850-983-5360 www.santarosa.fl.gov/emergency
- Okaloosa County: 850-651-7150 or myokaloosa.com/emergency-management
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Mobile AL around 4 AM CDT, or sooner if conditions warrant.
